subject: paper:hoogman-creativity-2020
quote: Most studies find evidence for increased divergent thinking for those with high ADHD scores (subclinical) but not for those with the disorder (clinical).
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). The crucial nuance: the divergent-thinking advantage is a trait-level effect, not present in clinical ADHD.

subject: paper:hoogman-creativity-2020
quote: We found no evidence for increased convergent thinking abilities in ADHD, nor did we find an overall negative effect of psychostimulants on creativity.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Bounds the effect (no convergent-thinking boost) and answers a common worry — stimulants do not overall reduce creativity.

subject: paper:hoogman-creativity-2020
quote: The rates of creative abilities/achievements were high among both clinical and subclinical groups.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Real-world creative achievement is elevated across both clinical and subclinical ADHD, distinct from the trait-specific divergent-thinking task effect.

subject: paper:boot-2020
quote: Adults with ADHD reported more real-world creative achievements.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Empirical replication of elevated real-world creative achievement in adults with ADHD.

subject: paper:boot-2020
quote: Our findings suggest that goal-directed motivation may drive the enhanced real-world creative achievements of people with ADHD.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Attributes the creative achievement to goal-directed motivation — connecting creativity to the reward/motivation mechanism rather than a free-standing gift.
